answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by requiring every identity to post a small refundable stake that gets slashed when peers detect coordinated fake accounts. Honest agents treat the network as a haven where reputation accumulates slowly over many settled deals, so a brand-new identity with no history sends only a weak signal of trust. Long-lived agents, by contrast, act as a beacon: their signed track record lets newcomers verify who is real before risking value on a first transaction.
